evidence.claim: The Egyptian president is the head of state and head of executive power under article 139 of the constitution.
evidence.title: President of the Republic
evidence.excerpt: The Egyptian president is the head of state and head of executive power under article 139 of the constitution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official constitutional summary from the Egyptian state information service; the office definition is stable across 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Stable constitutional authority in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s office, but not any specific 2022 action.
contrary_evidence: Constitutional authority alone does not show direct control over every security or nuclear decision.

evidence.claim: The report says Egypt faced credible reports of unlawful killings, state-security enforced disappearances, torture, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary arrest and detention, serious restrictions on assembly and expression, and weak accountability for security-force abuses.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The report says Egypt faced credible reports of unlawful killings, state-security enforced disappearances, torture, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary arrest and detention, serious restrictions on assembly and expression, and weak accountability for security-force abuses.
evidence.source_locator: Executive summary lines 44-45 and section 1 lines 49-50, 68-75, 95-100
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative U.S. government reporting with detailed 2022 coverage, mirrored by ecoi.net.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Applies to Sisi-era state institutions and security services; not every incident is proven to have been personally ordered by him.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some pardoned or released detainees, but says abuse remained pervasive.
Country-report format aggregates many incidents rather than proving command chains.

evidence.claim: The report says Sisi ended the formal state of emergency in 2021 but kept similar powers in place, and in April 2022 he reactivated the Presidential Pardon Commission, which led to releases of political prisoners through year-end.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The report says Sisi ended the formal state of emergency in 2021 but kept similar powers in place, and in April 2022 he reactivated the Presidential Pardon Commission, which led to releases of political prisoners through year-end.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same authoritative country report, with a specific 2022 institutional-change claim.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 legal and detention practice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi as president, though the report does not show how far he personally directed each release.
contrary_evidence: Reactivation of a pardon mechanism did not end arbitrary detention or abuse.
Retaining similar emergency powers cuts against a strong-restraint reading.

evidence.claim: Amnesty says Egyptian authorities arrested hundreds over protest calls, at least 151 people were under investigation, 1540 had been investigated for expression or association, many release orders were ignored, and COP27 protest rules required 36 hours' notice and restricted protests to a monitored area.
evidence.title: مصر: الاعتقالات بسبب دعوات التظاهر خلال مؤتمر المناخ تكشف واقع الأزمة الحقوقية
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty says Egyptian authorities arrested hundreds over protest calls, at least 151 people were under investigation, 1540 had been investigated for expression or association, many release orders were ignored, and COP27 protest rules required 36 hours' notice and restricted protests to a monitored area.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring with specific counts, named practices, and direct Arabic-language reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sisi-era protest policing and deterrence around a flagship international event.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty also notes some prisoners were released after the pardon committee was reactivated, so the picture is not pure one-way repression.
The article relies heavily on lawyers and civil-society reporting, though it cross-checks with documents and interviews.

evidence.claim: HRW says Egyptian authorities detained hundreds across the country after calls for anti-government protests, including journalists, lawyers, opposition figures, and activists.
evidence.title: مصر: اعتقالات وقمع إثر دعوات للاحتجاج
evidence.excerpt: HRW says Egyptian authorities detained hundreds across the country after calls for anti-government protests, including journalists, lawyers, opposition figures, and activists.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent corroboration from a major rights organization, but still a short news release rather than a full investigation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national security environment under Sisi, especially around COP27.
contrary_evidence: Short press release with less detail than a full report.
It overlaps with Amnesty’s account, so it mainly corroborates rather than adds new factual depth.

evidence.claim: Egypt released 3,273 inmates under presidential pardons after Sisi reactivated the Presidential Pardon Committee.
evidence.title: Egypt releases 3,273 prisoners granted presidential pardons on occasion of Sinai Liberation
evidence.excerpt: Egypt released 3,273 inmates under presidential pardons after Sisi reactivated the Presidential Pardon Committee.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable Egyptian outlet with a concrete outcome number, though it largely relays official action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi’s pardon decision and the committee’s operation.
contrary_evidence: The release affected some inmates but did not end arbitrary detention, torture, or protest repression.
The report is about pardons and release counts, not due process reform at large.

evidence.claim: AFTE said Egyptian authorities continued to restrict press and media in 2022, documenting 47 incidents and at least 63 violations, including arrests, blocking independent news websites, and judicial pressure on journalists.
evidence.title: Violations overshadow reform pledges.. The annual report on the state of freedom of expression in Egypt 2022
evidence.publisher: Association of Freedom of Thought and Expression
evidence.excerpt: AFTE said Egyptian authorities continued to restrict press and media in 2022, documenting 47 incidents and at least 63 violations, including arrests, blocking independent news websites, and judicial pressure on journalists.
evidence.source_locator: introduction and 'Second: Freedom of the press and media' section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed monitoring report built from AFTE casework and testimony, with concrete counts and categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government and its security/media apparatus.
contrary_evidence: The report notes some releases through the pardon committee.
It is a monitoring report from a rights NGO, so it emphasizes abuse rather than state rationale.

evidence.claim: AFTE documented 14 incidents containing at least 28 digital-rights violations in Q3 2022 and said the authorities continued to track and monitor citizens' social-media posts, especially those critical of the government.
evidence.title: No progress: the third quarterly report on the state of freedom of expression in Egypt (1 July - 30 September 2022)
evidence.publisher: Association of Freedom of Thought and Expression
evidence.excerpt: AFTE documented 14 incidents containing at least 28 digital-rights violations in Q3 2022 and said the authorities continued to track and monitor citizens' social-media posts, especially those critical of the government.
evidence.source_locator: Section Three: Digital rights and key patterns of violations
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous monitoring report with explicit digital-rights documentation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Egyptian authorities under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: AFTE documents patterns and cases, not a formal command memo.
The report covers one quarter, so it supports pattern evidence rather than a complete annual tally by itself.

evidence.claim: CPJ said state security forces arrested journalist Ahmed Fayez on November 10, 2022, after a Facebook post about Alaa Abdelfattah, and charged him with spreading false news and terrorism-related offenses.
evidence.title: Egyptian authorities arrest journalist Ahmed Fayez for reporting on Alaa Abdelfattah
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said state security forces arrested journalist Ahmed Fayez on November 10, 2022, after a Facebook post about Alaa Abdelfattah, and charged him with spreading false news and terrorism-related offenses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific named case from a leading press-freedom monitor, with detailed contemporaneous reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sisi-era security practice against critical journalists.
contrary_evidence: The account relies partly on local reporting and anonymous corroboration.
It is a single case, though it fits a broader pattern.

evidence.claim: CPJ said Alaa Abdelfattah had been imprisoned since 2019 and escalated his hunger strike ahead of COP27, with more than 60 civil-society organizations calling for his release.
evidence.title: CPJ joins call for release of Egyptian journalist Alaa Abdelfattah as he escalates hunger strike
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said Alaa Abdelfattah had been imprisoned since 2019 and escalated his hunger strike ahead of COP27, with more than 60 civil-society organizations calling for his release.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Strong contemporaneous advocacy and incident reporting, though not an investigative finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to the Sisi government because the detention and prison conditions were state-controlled.
contrary_evidence: This is a press-freedom campaign statement rather than a neutral audit.
It supports the broader repression pattern rather than proving a specific new 2022 action by Sisi.

evidence.claim: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and increase private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.title: Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.excerpt: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and increase private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential-office announcement on the exact date of adoption.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as president and policy sponsor.
contrary_evidence: The announcement does not prove effective implementation in 2022.
State ownership policies can be mixed if strategic-state carveouts are broad.

evidence.claim: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had built a vast economic portfolio under Sisi's state-led strategy and that its privileged access and opacity reproduced favoritism, patronage, and weak private-sector development.
evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt’s Military Economy
evidence.excerpt: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had built a vast economic portfolio under Sisi's state-led strategy and that its privileged access and opacity reproduced favoritism, patronage, and weak private-sector development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Serious policy scholarship with explicit evidence-based critique of the military economy and its incentives.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is inherited-structure context under Sisi, not a single 2022 choice, but it matters for judging his economic room to maneuver.
contrary_evidence: The paper also acknowledges some public benefits from military-managed infrastructure and housing.
Its argument is analytical and critical, so it should be balanced against official reform claims.

evidence.claim: The State Department said SOEs and military-owned companies enjoyed significant advantages, many SOEs received tax exemptions, and the December 29, 2022 State Ownership Policy aimed to reduce the government's role and raise private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent.
evidence.title: Egypt - United States Department of State
evidence.excerpt: The State Department said SOEs and military-owned companies enjoyed significant advantages, many SOEs received tax exemptions, and the December 29, 2022 State Ownership Policy aimed to reduce the government's role and raise private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent.
evidence.source_locator: Transparency of the Regulatory System and Privatization Program sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: U.S. government investment-climate assessment with a direct retrospective description of the 2022 policy baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Describes the structure and policy posture under Sisi's government, including military-linked advantages.
contrary_evidence: This is a 2024 retrospective, not a contemporaneous 2022 report.
The source emphasizes reform needs and thus frames the baseline critically.

evidence.claim: The cabinet announced that President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.title: Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet announced that President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential/cabinet announcement of a named policy document and its stated purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as a presidential approval, but still only a formal policy commitment rather than evidence of implementation or ethical restraint.
contrary_evidence: Later reporting and scholarship still described privileged state and military economic roles and limited private-sector opening.

evidence.claim: The paper argues that the military spearheaded Sisi's state-led investment strategy, controlled a vast economic portfolio, and benefited from privileged access and opacity that distorted private-sector development.
evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.excerpt: The paper argues that the military spearheaded Sisi's state-led investment strategy, controlled a vast economic portfolio, and benefited from privileged access and opacity that distorted private-sector development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-cited policy paper from a major think tank that gives a direct, source-based analysis of Egypt's military economy.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective analysis of the Sisi-era economy that directly covers the 2022 ruler-period context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The paper directly ties the state-led strategy to Sisi's presidency, but the evidence is systemic and network-based rather than a forensic finding of personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The same paper notes that some military projects did deliver public works, housing, and logistics benefits.
The same paper notes that some military projects delivered public works, housing, and logistics benefits.

evidence.claim: Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor during the currency crisis; Abdalla came from state-owned media leadership and had long banking experience.
evidence.title: Egypt's Sisi names Hassan Abdalla as caretaker cbank head
evidence.excerpt: Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker central bank governor during the currency crisis; Abdalla came from state-owned media leadership and had long banking experience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated reporting gives a direct account of the presidential appointment and the appointee's background.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a direct presidential appointment and therefore attributable to Sisi; the appointee's banking background limits any simple nepotism inference.
contrary_evidence: Abdalla was also described as a veteran banker with relevant experience, so the appointment is not proof of cronyism or incompetence.

evidence.claim: HRW said the Egyptian government failed to ease repression in 2022 or repeal laws curtailing basic freedoms, while civil society faced travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal investigations in retaliation for peaceful activism and criticism.
evidence.title: Egypt: A Year of Whitewashing Despite Dire Crisis
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the Egyptian government failed to ease repression in 2022 or repeal laws curtailing basic freedoms, while civil society faced travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal investigations in retaliation for peaceful activism and criticism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: HRW's year-end news release directly summarizes its World Report findings and names the main mechanisms of repression.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The pattern is tied to Sisi's government and the institutions he oversees; the release does not prove personal orders in every case, but it does show tolerated, repeated abuse under his rule.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes the government's national dialogue and COP27 efforts, but treats them as mostly cosmetic whitewashing rather than real restraint.

evidence.claim: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities reached a staff-level agreement on a 46-month EFF whose package aimed to safeguard macroeconomic stability, strengthen the social safety net, reduce the state footprint, and improve governance and transparency.
evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities reached a staff-level agreement on a 46-month EFF whose package aimed to safeguard macroeconomic stability, strengthen the social safety net, reduce the state footprint, and improve governance and transparency.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release describing the agreed policy package and quoting the mission chief.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The agreement concerns policies publicly backed by Sisi's government; it is attributable as an official commitment, not as proof of personal candor or self-dealing.
contrary_evidence: AFTE later argued the government's reform language did not translate into a real opening and that implementation remained selective.

evidence.claim: The IMF approved Egypt's EFF and said the program would restore buffers, reduce the state footprint, strengthen governance and transparency, and support social safety nets and private-sector-led growth.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Approves 46-month US$3 billion Extended Arrangement for Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The IMF approved Egypt's EFF and said the program would restore buffers, reduce the state footprint, strengthen governance and transparency, and support social safety nets and private-sector-led growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release with detailed program language and the Board approval announcement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a formal policy commitment made under Sisi's presidency and his government; it does not itself prove personal honesty or separation from interests.
contrary_evidence: The approval does not by itself show that implementation overcame entrenched state and military privileges.

evidence.claim: AFTE said the government's 2022 reform language was empty rhetoric and that security and judicial practices continued to persecute opinion-makers, journalists, and creators; it documented 47 incidents with at least 63 violations against the press and media community in 2022.
evidence.title: Violations overshadow reform pledges.. The annual report on the state of freedom of expression in Egypt 2022
evidence.publisher: Association of Freedom of Thought and Expression
evidence.excerpt: AFTE said the government's 2022 reform language was empty rhetoric and that security and judicial practices continued to persecute opinion-makers, journalists, and creators; it documented 47 incidents with at least 63 violations against the press and media community in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report is advocacy-oriented but provides specific case documentation, counts, and contemporaneous monitoring notes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report attributes the pattern to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's presidency; it does not prove he personally ordered each case, but repeated notice and lack of correction support ruler attribution.
contrary_evidence: The pardon committee did release some detainees, which AFTE treats as limited and selective corrective action.

evidence.claim: AFTE documented at least 59 violations in the third quarter of 2022, said the national dialogue had not become a real opening, and reported that the pardon committee released 520 political detainees and 13 convicts but with slow, selective results controlled in part by security bodies.
evidence.title: No progress | The third quarterly report on the state of freedom of expression in Egypt (1 July - 30 September 2022)
evidence.publisher: Association of Freedom of Thought and Expression
evidence.excerpt: AFTE documented at least 59 violations in the third quarter of 2022, said the national dialogue had not become a real opening, and reported that the pardon committee released 520 political detainees and 13 convicts but with slow, selective results controlled in part by security bodies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Quarterly monitoring report with named counts and process details; advocacy framing is present but the underlying documentation is specific.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The dialogue and pardon committee were created or reactivated by Sisi, but the report says security apparatuses still controlled key outcomes, which limits claims of genuine self-binding.
contrary_evidence: The same report confirms that the president did call for dialogue and reactivate the pardon committee, so the record is mixed rather than purely negative.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Egyptian authorities arrested hundreds of people over protest calls before COP27, with at least 151 detainees under investigation and about 1,540 people investigated for free speech and association; it urged President al-Sisi to release those arbitrarily held.
evidence.title: Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Egyptian authorities arrested hundreds of people over protest calls before COP27, with at least 151 detainees under investigation and about 1,540 people investigated for free speech and association; it urged President al-Sisi to release those arbitrarily held.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Amnesty's press release is specific about the detention campaign, counts, and the timeline immediately before COP27.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrests were carried out by Egyptian authorities under Sisi's presidency in a highly visible national-security setting; direct presidential orders are not shown for each arrest, but the pattern is ruler-attributable through tolerance and notice.
contrary_evidence: Authorities also used the pardon committee and released some prisoners, but Amnesty says that did not offset the wider detention campaign.

evidence.claim: CPJ said state security forces arrested journalist Ahmed Fayez after a Facebook post reporting that prison authorities were force-feeding Alaa Abdelfattah; Fayez was charged with false-news and terrorism-related offenses and held pending trial.
evidence.title: Egyptian authorities arrest journalist Ahmed Fayez for reporting on Alaa Abdelfattah
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said state security forces arrested journalist Ahmed Fayez after a Facebook post reporting that prison authorities were force-feeding Alaa Abdelfattah; Fayez was charged with false-news and terrorism-related offenses and held pending trial.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: CPJ identifies the arresting authority, the precipitating post, and the charges in a contemporaneous alert.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a direct state-security and prosecutorial action under Sisi's presidency; the report does not prove he personally ordered the arrest, but it is strong evidence of tolerated retaliation against truth-telling.
contrary_evidence: The case arose from a journalist reporting on prison abuse rather than any proven false allegation about private conduct.

evidence.claim: CPJ said Egyptian authorities had detained three journalists since September 2022 and warned that the arrests showed little concern for protecting journalists ahead of COP27.
evidence.title: Egyptian authorities detain 3 journalists since September
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said Egyptian authorities had detained three journalists since September 2022 and warned that the arrests showed little concern for protecting journalists ahead of COP27.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: CPJ's contemporaneous alert names the journalists and the timing, and it is closely tied to the COP27 crackdown context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrests were made by Egyptian security forces during Sisi's presidency; the source supports a ruler-attributable pattern of intimidation rather than a single isolated case.
contrary_evidence: The government publicly framed COP27 as a normal diplomatic event, but CPJ says the arrests undercut that claim.

evidence.claim: Egypt announced the release of 3,273 inmates under presidential pardon, and the move was presented as implementation of Sisi's decision to reactivate the Presidential Pardon Committee.
evidence.title: Egypt releases 3,273 prisoners granted presidential pardons on occasion of Sinai Liberation
evidence.excerpt: Egypt announced the release of 3,273 inmates under presidential pardon, and the move was presented as implementation of Sisi's decision to reactivate the Presidential Pardon Committee.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Ahram is state-affiliated and reliable for reporting the official decree and release count, though it is not independent on motive or broader evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The pardon decision is directly attributable to Sisi, but the article also shows the action was procedural and selective rather than a broad transparency reform.
contrary_evidence: AFTE later said the pardon process remained slow, selective, and security-controlled, so the release does not by itself establish sustained accountability.

evidence.claim: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities agreed on a 46-month EFF package built around macroeconomic stabilization, debt sustainability, a stronger social safety net, and reforms to support private-sector-led growth and job creation.
evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff and Egyptian authorities agreed on a 46-month EFF package built around macroeconomic stabilization, debt sustainability, a stronger social safety net, and reforms to support private-sector-led growth and job creation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release announcing the agreed package and its stated policy goals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Egyptian authorities under Sisi's presidency as the agreed program framework, but it is a commitment rather than proof of execution.
contrary_evidence: The agreement itself does not show that the reforms were fully implemented during 2022.

evidence.claim: The staff report says Egypt's program rests on three pillars: exchange-rate and monetary policy to restore resilience, fiscal discipline to keep debt on a downward path while protecting social spending, and broad structural reforms to reduce the state footprint and level the playing field; it also says the agenda includes publishing a President-endorsed state ownership policy and an ambitious divestment plan.
evidence.title: Arab Republic of Egypt: Request for Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The staff report says Egypt's program rests on three pillars: exchange-rate and monetary policy to restore resilience, fiscal discipline to keep debt on a downward path while protecting social spending, and broad structural reforms to reduce the state footprint and level the playing field; it also says the agenda includes publishing a President-endorsed state ownership policy and an ambitious divestment plan.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph 9 and the SOE reforms section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IMF staff report with specific program design and implementation commitments, though retrospective to the late-2022 package.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective description of the late-2022 program and implementation framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The program is the government's, not a private staff memo; it is attributable to Sisi's administration but still not a direct record of his personal decision-making.
contrary_evidence: The report frames these as commitments and mechanisms, not as completed outcomes inside 2022.

evidence.claim: The FY 2021/22 social welfare plan allocated EGP 283.4 billion to social protection and set targets including extending safety nets to poor and vulnerable groups, reaching 4 million poor families, covering 18 million workers with social insurance, and increasing pensions.
evidence.title: Egypt’s Ministry of Planning and Economic Development announces pillars of 21/2022 social welfare plan
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Planning and Economic Development
evidence.excerpt: The FY 2021/22 social welfare plan allocated EGP 283.4 billion to social protection and set targets including extending safety nets to poor and vulnerable groups, reaching 4 million poor families, covering 18 million workers with social insurance, and increasing pensions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry plan with budget figures and target outputs stated contemporaneously.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects state planning under Sisi's government, but the document is a plan and target set, not a full execution audit.
contrary_evidence: The same page presents these as plan targets and projected effects, not independently verified outcomes.

evidence.claim: The FY 2022/23 draft budget allocated EGP 302.2 billion to social protection, including support for Takaful and Karama, housing, and home-gas connection, while the ministry said the policy package was intended to keep poverty trending downward.
evidence.title: Gov’t allocates EGP 302 billion to support social welfare in the state’s FY 2022/2023 plan: Planning Minister
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Planning and Economic Development
evidence.excerpt: The FY 2022/23 draft budget allocated EGP 302.2 billion to social protection, including support for Takaful and Karama, housing, and home-gas connection, while the ministry said the policy package was intended to keep poverty trending downward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry budget-planning announcement with named allocations and targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State budget planning under Sisi's presidency, but still a budget plan and target statement rather than proof of realized results.
contrary_evidence: The document itself treats the poverty figures as goals or expected direction rather than audited end-year outcomes.

evidence.claim: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects, and the government said it would put the document into force immediately.
evidence.title: Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.excerpt: President Abdel Fattah El Sisi approved the State Ownership Policy Document, which was meant to define the state's relation with the private sector and expand private-sector participation in development projects, and the government said it would put the document into force immediately.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official announcement of a named presidential approval and its immediate policy effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable as a presidential approval, but still only a formal policy commitment rather than an implementation audit.
contrary_evidence: The announcement does not by itself show that the policy was enforced across state-owned and military-linked entities during 2022.

evidence.claim: A Saudi sovereign-wealth-fund unit bought minority stakes in four Egyptian listed companies for $1.3 billion, showing that the government's asset-sale and private-capital program had moved from announcement to execution in 2022.
evidence.title: Saudi Arabia’s $10 Billion Pledge to Egypt Delivers First Deals
evidence.excerpt: A Saudi sovereign-wealth-fund unit bought minority stakes in four Egyptian listed companies for $1.3 billion, showing that the government's asset-sale and private-capital program had moved from announcement to execution in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced Bloomberg reporting with a specific transaction, buyer, value, and target companies.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The transaction was executed by state-linked Egyptian entities under the government's program, not by Sisi personally, but it is strong evidence of ruler-attributable implementation.
contrary_evidence: It is a minority-stake sale in four firms, so it does not prove broader private-sector rebalancing on its own.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said foreign-exchange buffers had fallen sharply since March 2022, the Central Bank allowed depreciation and raised rates, the government announced social mitigation packages, growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23, and poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said foreign-exchange buffers had fallen sharply since March 2022, the Central Bank allowed depreciation and raised rates, the government announced social mitigation packages, growth was expected to slow to 4.5 percent in FY2022/23, and poverty could increase because inflation was eroding real incomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral assessment summarizing contemporaneous policy responses and their likely effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: These measures are attributable to the CBE and government under Sisi's administration, but the report also makes clear that external shocks materially constrained choices.
contrary_evidence: The same monitor notes that gas extractives, communications, agriculture, and construction were still performing relatively well, and FY2021/22 growth had rebounded strongly.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of Sisi personally making a 2022 nuclear-safety, command-and-control, or crisis-escalation choice.
Concrete durable-conflict outcomes are thin beyond mediation and de-escalatory posture.
Exact chains of command and the effectiveness of pardon/reform mechanisms remain opaque.
There was no 2022 election, so contestability and transfer-rule evidence remains mostly structural rather than event-based.
Household-level distribution and implementation depth of the reform package are still thin.
Independent 2022 household outcome data are still thin, especially on whether transfers and pensions offset inflation.
There is no direct 2022 asset declaration, audit trail, procurement finding, or court judgment tying Sisi or close family to specific private gain from office.
Direct truthfulness/correction evidence from Sisi's own statements is still thin.
Direct evidence of Sisi's personal steering of tactical adjustments and durable outcome attribution remains limited.
